## Deploy

Live at **https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud** (Hostinger VPS, Ubuntu 24.04, Docker).
The VPS's Docker Manager already runs Traefik on :80/:443 with Let's Encrypt, so our Caddy sits
behind it (`deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml`). From any checkout with the deploy SSH key:

```bash
git fetch && HOSTINGER_HOST=srv2159172.hstgr.cloud HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY=REDACTED \
  CHECK_URL=https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud \
  deploy/deploy.sh                      # default ref: origin/main; pass a sha to roll back
deploy/check.sh                         # outside check: health + ingest lag, clusters, metrics, web
curl https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/version.txt   # deployed commit
```

Redeploy after every merge to `main`. `deploy/check.sh` also runs every 5 minutes from the team
server (cron of the deploying user) and logs to `~/noise-radar-health.log`.

Running it on the VPS: every long-running service has `restart: unless-stopped` (`migrate` is a
one-shot and exits). Raw Jetstream tables keep `INGEST_RETENTION_HOURS` of data (likes:
`INGEST_LIKES_RETENTION_HOURS`), set in the VPS `.env`; at ~0.7 GB/hour of raw rows that bounds the
database, and anything a cluster references is copied to `cluster_posts_snapshot` first. The signals
worker gets 4G on the VPS (`docker-compose.hostinger.yml`) because the 1h window needs more than 2G.

`deploy.sh` ships the committed tree with `git archive` (the VPS has no GitHub access) into
`/opt/noise-radar/releases/<sha>`, points `current` at it and runs compose. Secrets live only in
`/opt/noise-radar/.env` on the VPS (same names as `.env.example`); edit it there, then redeploy.

On a plain VPS without Traefik, drop the override and set `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` so Caddy gets HTTPS itself:
`docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build`.

All backend services share one image (`Dockerfile`); add a service in compose with its own
`command` (e.g. `python -m ingest`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ship a committed git ref to the Hostinger VPS and (re)start the stack there.
#   deploy/deploy.sh [ref]          # default: origin/main (run `git fetch` first)
# Env: HOSTINGER_HOST (required), HOSTINGER_USER (default root), HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY (optional key file),
#      HOSTINGER_DIR (default /opt/noise-radar), CHECK_URL (public base URL; when set, deploy/check.sh
#      runs against it after the deploy and the script fails if the site is unhealthy).
# The VPS needs no GitHub access: the tree goes over SSH with `git archive`, so only committed files
# ship. Each deploy lands in $DIR/releases/<sha>, `current` points at it, and $DIR/.env (created once
# by hand on the VPS, never committed) is linked into every release. Roll back: deploy an older sha.
set -euo pipefail

ref=${1:-origin/main}
host=${HOSTINGER_HOST:?set HOSTINGER_HOST}
user=${HOSTINGER_USER:-root}
dir=${HOSTINGER_DIR:-/opt/noise-radar}
ssh_opts=(-o BatchMode=yes)
if [[ -n ${HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY:-} ]]; then ssh_opts+=(-i "$HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes); fi

sha=$(git rev-parse --short=12 "$ref^{commit}")
echo "deploying $ref ($sha) to $user@$host:$dir"

# 1) upload the tree into releases/<sha>.tmp, unless that release is already on the VPS
if ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" "test -d '$dir/releases/$sha'"; then
  echo "release $sha already on the VPS, skipping upload"
else
  git archive --format=tar "$sha" | ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" \
    "set -e; rm -rf '$dir/releases/$sha.tmp'; mkdir -p '$dir/releases/$sha.tmp'; tar -x -C '$dir/releases/$sha.tmp'"
fi

# 2) build, start, and only then point `current` at it
ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" bash -s -- "$dir" "$sha" <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
dir=$1 sha=$2
rel=$dir/releases/$sha
test -f "$dir/.env" || { echo "missing $dir/.env on the VPS (copy .env.example and fill it in)" >&2; exit 1; }
exec 9>"$dir/.deploy.lock"
flock -w 600 9 || { echo "another deploy is running" >&2; exit 1; }
if [[ -d $rel.tmp ]]; then
  ln -sfn ../../.env "$rel.tmp/.env"
  echo "$sha" > "$rel.tmp/web/public/version.txt"
  rm -rf "$rel" && mv "$rel.tmp" "$rel"
fi
touch "$rel"   # newest mtime, so pruning below never removes the live release
# Run compose from the real release path (not the `current` symlink): bind-mount paths then change
# per release, so compose recreates the containers that mount repo files (Caddy, db init script).
cd "$rel"
dc=(docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml --env-file .env)
"${dc[@]}" build
"${dc[@]}" up -d --remove-orphans
ln -sfn "releases/$sha" "$dir/current"
docker image prune -f --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=noise-radar >/dev/null
docker builder prune -f --filter until=72h >/dev/null   # build cache grows ~1 GB per deploy otherwise
# keep the 5 newest finished releases
ls -1dt "$dir"/releases/*/ | { grep -v '\.tmp/$' || true; } | tail -n +6 | xargs -r rm -rf
"${dc[@]}" ps
REMOTE

if [[ -n ${CHECK_URL:-} ]]; then
  for _ in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do   # api and ingest need a moment after a recreate
    if "$(dirname "$0")/check.sh" "$CHECK_URL"; then exit 0; fi
    sleep 15
  done
  echo "deployed $sha, but $CHECK_URL is unhealthy" >&2
  exit 1
fi

## Workflow with Entire

- One Trail per feature: from your feature branch run `entire trail create --title "<what and why>" --type feature`. Commits pushed to that branch, and the agent sessions behind them, attach to the Trail.
- Commit agent work with the agent running, so Entire links the commit to its session (`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer). Don't amend or rebase away those trailers.
- Before merging, run `entire review general`. It reviews locally with Claude Code (no Entire credit; Codex-only users ask a teammate to run it) and posts the verdict to the Trail. Fix or dismiss each finding, then open the PR with `entire trail ci-pr`, undraft it with `entire trail ready`, and squash-merge it while keeping the checkpoint trailers in the squash commit:

  ```bash
  gh pr merge <n> --squash --body "$(git log --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)' origin/main..HEAD | grep . | sort -u)"
  ```

  A squash without those trailers loses the link between the commit on `main` and its agent sessions.
- Don't run `entire trail rerun-review` or enable project Agents on entire.com: those run paid cloud agents. Ask the repo owner first.
- Never paste keys or `.env` contents into a prompt: transcripts are stored in checkpoints.

"""Apply the DB schema: db/schema.sql, then db/migrations/*.sql in name order.

    python -m common.migrate              # uses DATABASE_URL
    python -m common.migrate --url postgresql://...

Every file is idempotent, so re-running is safe. Applied migration names are recorded in
`schema_migrations` and skipped next time; db/schema.sql (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS) always runs.
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import psycopg

from common.config import get_settings

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SCHEMA = ROOT / "db" / "schema.sql"
MIGRATIONS = ROOT / "db" / "migrations"


def migrate(url: str) -> list[str]:
    applied_now: list[str] = []
    with psycopg.connect(url, autocommit=True) as conn:
        conn.execute(SCHEMA.read_text())
        done: set[str] = set()
        if conn.execute("SELECT to_regclass('schema_migrations')").fetchone()[0]:
            done = {r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT name FROM schema_migrations")}
        for path in sorted(MIGRATIONS.glob("*.sql")):
            if path.name in done:
                continue
            with conn.transaction():
                conn.execute(path.read_text())
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO schema_migrations (name) VALUES (%s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
                    (path.name,),
                )
            applied_now.append(path.name)
    return applied_now


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--url", default=None, help="Postgres URL (default: DATABASE_URL)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    applied = migrate(args.url or get_settings().database_url)
    print("applied:", ", ".join(applied) if applied else "nothing new", file=sys.stderr)
